issues.legal_issue: A bare claim of tenancy unsupported by material particulars does not justify framing a tenancy issue for referral to the tenancy authority in execution proceedings.
material_facts: The trustees sought execution of a scheme treated as a decree to recover trust land from a former trustee.
In a joint application in the execution proceedings, a respondent claimed to be a tenant but gave no particulars of when or how the tenancy arose, who created it, or its terms.
The tenancy authority’s earlier suo motu proceedings had been dropped because the trust land was exempt; those proceedings had not determined whether the respondent was a tenant.
issues.conclusion: The execution court rightly rejected the tenancy objection. The High Court should not have directed that a tenancy issue be framed and referred to the Tehsildar.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VI Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, pleadings must state the material facts relied on. A tenancy issue cannot be raised on a vague plea lacking particulars of the tenancy and the right claimed. The Court applied Ram Sarup Gupta v. Bishun Narain Inter College (1987) 2 SCC 555, which requires essential material facts while directing courts to consider the substance rather than the form of pleadings; M/s Nilesh Construction Company v. M/s Gangubai, AIR 1982 Bombay 491, which requires particulars before referral of a tenancy issue; and Pandu Dhondi Yerudkar v. Ananda Krishna Patil, 1947 (76) BLR 368, which identifies particulars such as when and by whom a tenancy was created and its terms. The earlier case also recognized that an issue already raised must be referred, but no such adequately supported issue arose here. Section 125 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands (Vidarbha Region) Act, 1958, was the provision under which the High Court directed referral.

predicates.execution_of_trust_scheme: The proceeding is execution of a scheme governing trust property that is treated as a decree.
predicates.tenancy_claim_lacks_material_particulars: A party claims tenancy but does not state facts such as when or how it arose, who created it, or its terms.
predicates.tenancy_issue_referral_not_justified: A tenancy issue should not be framed for referral to the tenancy authority on the unsupported claim alone.

issues.definition: When execution of a trust scheme is opposed by a tenancy claim lacking material particulars, the claim alone does not justify referring a tenancy issue.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional court should not overturn the execution courts’ rejection of a tenancy objection or direct transfer of trust property when the tenancy plea has no factual basis.
material_facts: The execution court rejected the respondents’ objection, and the trust obtained possession of the land through execution.
The District Judge dismissed the appeal from the execution court’s orders.
The High Court accepted that the scheme could be executed as a decree but directed referral of a tenancy issue and ordered the trust to hand possession to the claimant.
The tenancy claim lacked material particulars, and the earlier tenancy-authority proceedings had not determined the claimant’s tenancy status.
issues.conclusion: The High Court ought not to have interfered in revision without a factual basis for the tenancy plea. Its directions referring the issue and requiring transfer of possession were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that revisional interference was unwarranted in the circumstances because the tenancy plea had no supporting factual basis. The pleading principles in Order VI Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as discussed in Ram Sarup Gupta v. Bishun Narain Inter College (1987) 2 SCC 555, and the requirement of particulars reflected in M/s Nilesh Construction Company v. M/s Gangubai, AIR 1982 Bombay 491, supported that conclusion. The Court also relied on Pandu Dhondi Yerudkar v. Ananda Krishna Patil, 1947 (76) BLR 368, concerning the particulars needed for a tenancy plea.

predicates.revision_proceeding_from_execution: A revisional court is reviewing orders made in execution proceedings.
predicates.lower_courts_rejected_tenancy_objection: The execution court rejected the tenancy objection and the appellate court left that rejection undisturbed.
predicates.tenancy_claim_lacks_factual_basis: The party claiming tenancy provides no material facts supporting how the tenancy arose or what its terms were.
predicates.revisional_interference_unwarranted: The revisional court should not interfere with the execution courts’ orders on the unsupported tenancy claim.

issues.definition: When a revision concerns execution orders, the lower courts rejected the tenancy objection, and the tenancy claim lacks factual support, revisional interference is unwarranted.
